16.0.0.en: 1 Again the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations, 3 And say, Thus saith the Lord GOD unto Jerusalem; Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of Canaan; thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother an Hittite. 4 And as for thy nativity, in the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed in water to supple thee; thou wast not salted at all, nor swaddled at all. 5 None eye pitied thee, to do any of these unto thee, to have compassion upon thee; but thou wast cast out in the open field, to the lothing of thy person, in the day that thou wast born. 6 And when I passed by thee, and saw thee polluted in thine own blood, I said unto thee when thou wast in thy blood, Live; yea, I said unto thee when thou wast in thy blood, Live.

16.1.0.en: If this chapter truly represents the song of the free salvation which God offered us in spite of our sins and the uncleanness of our hearts, and which He continues to offer us all the days of our exile until He brings us in as a holy bride of the Lord Christ, then the beginning of this song is "our discovery of our sins," that we may receive His work in us. The words of the Lord begin thus: "Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations" [2]. This is the way that St. John the Baptist prepared for the Lord Christ, when he came to reveal human weakness, so that sinners might accept the atoning sacrifice of Christ.

16.1.1.en: This is the work of the Holy Spirit in us: He exposes our weaknesses before our inner sight so that we confess them. As St. Anthony the Great says: [If the soul surrenders itself to the Lord with all its strength, the good God shows it these pains and defects one by one so that it may turn away from them]. And St. Ephrem the Syrian says: [You cannot listen to His words while you do not yet know yourself].

16.2.0.en: What are her abominations? "Say, Thus saith the Lord GOD unto Jerusalem; Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of Canaan; thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother an Hittite" [3]... Judah and also Israel boasted that they were of the seed of Abraham, a chosen race. But the Lord declares to Jerusalem that spiritually she did not come forth from the loins of Abraham nor was she born of him, but of the land of Canaan; her father was an Amorite and her mother a Hittite. They fell into the sins of the Amorites and the Hittites and were joined to them through evil, so their sonship to Abraham, the father of the believers, was taken away from them, and even their relationship to God was taken away, and they truly became the sons of these two peoples. As Tertullian says: [They are not of the descent of these two peoples, but they were called their children because of their likeness to their evil; these whom He formerly called His sons by the prophet Isaiah, saying, "I have nourished and brought up children" (Isa 2:1)]. And St. Augustine says: [Since the Amorites and the Hittites were wicked, and the Jews imitated them in their evil, they found in them parents, not because they were born of them but because they shared with them in their condemnation, having walked in their customs].

16.2.1.en: And Origen says: [Jerusalem committed such sins (the worship of idols) and does not deserve to enter into the promises of God]. She became a Canaanite, with an Amorite father and a Hittite mother, outside the circle of the divine promises. So whoever accepts strange teachings and false philosophies, far from the spirit of the Holy Bible, remains outside, and is not counted as the holy Jerusalem but as a Canaanite or an Amorite or a Hittite!

16.2.2.en: Origen observed that when rebuking Jerusalem the Lord mentioned that her father was of one nationality (Amorite) and her mother of another (Hittite), because where sin exists there is division, schism and separation, and where virtue exists there is unity. He says: [Where sins are, there is stumbling, separation, heresies and disputes; and where virtue is, there is unity and union, where the believers are of one heart and one soul. Let us say plainly that the root of evils is multiplicity and the beginning of goodness is to live in unity... so that we may be one body and one spirit. But if we are not united we say: I am of Paul, and I of Apollos, and I of Cephas... Besides this we are divided and separated, and we do not reach the place of those whom unity has gathered, and as the Father and the Son are one, so all who have one spirit are one].

16.3.0.en: As for the beginning of her committing abominations, it is as He says: "In the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed in water to supple thee; thou wast not salted at all, nor swaddled at all. None eye pitied thee, to do any of these unto thee, to have compassion upon thee; but thou wast cast out in the open field, to the lothing of thy person, in the day that thou wast born" [4-5]. The newborn child was gently rubbed with salt and swaddled, and his hands and feet were left swaddled for several days. Mothers believed that by this their children would become strong and be kept safe from any germ. This was the custom of the East in ancient times, so we hear that the Virgin swaddled the child Jesus.

16.3.1.en: That the child was not swaddled or salted means that he was an unwanted child. It is a painful picture of the whole human race, for man is born with his abominations working within him, and there is no one among men who can wash away his uncleanness, or cover him with a swaddling band, or carry him away from his shame! Therefore the Psalmist cries out, saying: "Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me" (Ps 51:5), and the prophet Jeremiah says: Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh (humanity) his arm, and whose heart departeth from the LORD" (Jer 17:5)... Thus man feels a complete inability to sanctify himself, with none to support him or help him, and so God Himself had to intervene.

16.3.2.en: Some of the Fathers see in the words "thy navel was not cut" a reference to the first sin, when Eve fell into gluttony and led her husband astray with her, and to the sin of preoccupation with eating and drinking into which the Jewish people fell, as the Apostle says: "As it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play" (1 Cor 10:7; Ex 32:6). St. John Chrysostom says: [Truly, Adam was driven out of Paradise after he failed to control his belly, and for the same reason the flood came in the days of Noah...]. He also says: [Neither the body nor food is from Satan, but luxury alone, for through it the wicked Satan brings forward his evils without number. By this he makes victims of all men]. St. Moses the Black says: [Know for certain that every man who eats and drinks without restraint and loves the vanities of this world cannot obtain anything of goodness, nor will he ever attain it, but he deceives himself]. And St. Isaac the Syrian says: [Sit with hyenas, but do not sit with the glutton who is never satisfied].

16.4.s.en: 2. God betroths her to Himself as a bride:

16.4.0.en: 7 I have caused thee to multiply as the bud of the field, and thou hast increased and waxen great, and thou art come to excellent ornaments: thy breasts are fashioned, and thine hair is grown, whereas thou wast naked and bare. 8 Now when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time was the time of love; and I spread my skirt over thee, and covered thy nakedness: yea, I sware unto thee, and entered into a covenant with thee, saith the Lord GOD, and thou becamest mine. 9 Then washed I thee with water; yea, I throughly washed away thy blood from thee, and I anointed thee with oil. 10 I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers' skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk. 11 I decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands, and a chain on thy neck. 12 And I put a jewel in thy nose, and earrings in thine ears, and a beautiful crown upon thine head. 13 Thus wast thou decked with gold and silver; and thy raiment was of fine linen, and silk, and broidered work; thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil: and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. 14 And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD.

16.4.1.en: The Lord affirms to the human soul: "When I passed by thee, and saw thee polluted in thine own blood... when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time was the time of love" [6-8]. The Lord passed by her and found her naked, with none to cover her. So He came to her in love and betrothed her to Himself as a bride: "I spread my skirt over thee, and covered thy nakedness: yea, I sware unto thee, and entered into a covenant with thee, saith the Lord GOD, and thou becamest mine" [8]. The Holy One did not disdain to come down to us in the land of misery, and to stretch out His hand to our weakness to grant us union with Him, offering Himself as a bridegroom to us, that we might be a bride to Him. Concerning this St. John Chrysostom says: [As I have said, He who is great and mighty desired a harlot, and I am speaking of human nature under that name "harlot." If a man desires a harlot he is condemned, so how does God desire a harlot, so as to become a bridegroom to her?! What does He do?! He did not send to her one of His servants, neither an angel, nor an archangel, nor a cherub, nor a seraph, but He Himself came down, He who loves her, drawing near to her... Since she was unable to ascend to the Most High, He came down to the earth; He came to the harlot and was not ashamed to take hold of her in her drunkenness... And how did He come? He came not (revealing) the essence of His nature in an abstract manner, but He became like the harlot (apart from sin), not in appearance but in truth He became like her, so that she might not tremble at Him when she saw Him and run away and flee!! He came to the harlot and became man!...].

16.5.0.en: "Then washed I thee with water; yea, I throughly washed away thy blood from thee, and I anointed thee with oil.

16.6.0.en: I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers' skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk. I decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands, and a chain on thy neck. And I put a jewel in thy nose, and earrings in thine ears, and a beautiful crown upon thine head. Thus wast thou decked with gold and silver; and thy raiment was of fine linen, and silk, and broidered work; thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil: and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD" [9-14].

16.6.1.en: It is a wonderful picture of the work of the Lord Christ with us, especially through the waters of Holy Baptism, the anointing of the Holy Myron, and the sacrament of the Eucharist. We have already interpreted this text in our book "The Holy Spirit between the New Birth and Continual Renewal."

16.6.2.en: He brought her into the waters of Holy Baptism to wash her from the blood of her sins [9]. As St. Augustine says: [By our birth of water and the Holy Spirit we are cleansed from every sin, whether from Adam, by whom all sinned, or by our own deed and word, for we are washed from them in Baptism]. He anoints her with the oil of holy anointing, so that by His Holy Spirit she becomes His possession, bearing the seal of the Spirit. He clothes her with the garments of righteousness, and shoes her to walk in the way of God. She wears fine linen, a sign of purity and chastity, and silk, a sign of righteousness. He gives her ornaments that are not of this world, but are the earnest of the Spirit that gives the soul beauty. He puts bracelets on her hands, a chain on her neck, a jewel in her nose, earrings in her ears and a beautiful crown on her head; these are nothing but the works of the Holy Spirit in our inner life, as He sanctifies all her senses and powers for the sake of the Kingdom, so that her hand is stretched out to work without sloth, her neck bends to carry the burdens of others with joy, her nose is opened to smell the fragrance of heaven, and her ears are adorned by hearing the divine commandments; and the crown of her beauty is the Lord Christ Himself, who fills her mind and directs all her conduct. This is the work of God in us! He gives us gold and silver, that is, He gives us "the heavenly life," which is indicated by gold, and the word of God, which is refined seven times like silver. He satisfies our souls with the holy Body and leaves us hungry for nothing! By this the soul becomes exceedingly beautiful and fit to enter the kingdom of her bridegroom as a queen adorned with the splendor of her perfect bridegroom, which He pours upon her, and she receives a name, the name of her holy Christ.

16.7.0.en: 15 "But thou didst trust in thine own beauty, and playedst the harlot because of thy renown, and pouredst out thy fornications on every one that passed by; his it was. 16 And of thy garments thou didst take, and deckedst thy high places with divers colours, and playedst the harlot thereupon: the like things shall not come, neither shall it be so. 17 Thou hast also taken thy fair jewels of my gold and of my silver, which I had given thee, and madest to thyself images of men, and didst commit whoredom with them, 18 And tookest thy broidered garments, and coverest them: and thou hast set mine oil and mine incense before them. 19 My meat also which I gave thee, fine flour, and oil, and honey, wherewith I fed thee, thou hast even set it before them for a sweet savour: and thus it was, saith the Lord GOD. 20 Moreover thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured. Is this of thy whoredoms a small matter, 21 That thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them? 22 And in all thine abominations and thy whoredoms thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, when thou wast naked and bare, and wast polluted in thy blood. 23 And it came to pass after all thy wickedness, (woe, woe unto thee! saith the Lord GOD;) 24 That thou hast also built unto thee an eminent place, and hast made thee an high place in every street. 25 Thou hast built thy high place at every head of the way, and hast made thy beauty to be abhorred, and hast opened thy feet to every one that passed by, and multiplied thy whoredoms. 26 Thou hast also committed fornication with the Egyptians thy neighbours, great of flesh; and hast increased thy whoredoms, to provoke me to anger. 27 Behold, therefore I have stretched out my hand over thee, and have withheld thine ordinary portion, and delivered thee unto the will of them that hate thee, the daughters of the Philistines, which are ashamed of thy lewd way. 28 Thou hast played the whore also with the Assyrians, because thou wast unsatiable; yea, thou hast played the harlot with them, and yet couldest not be satisfied. 29 Thou hast moreover multiplied thy fornication in the land of Canaan unto Chaldea; and yet thou wast not satisfied herewith. 30 How weak is thine heart, saith the Lord GOD, seeing thou doest all these things, the work of an imperious whorish woman; 31 In that thou buildest thine eminent place in the head of every way, and makest thine high place in every street; and hast not been as an harlot, in that thou scornest hire; 32 But as a wife that committeth adultery, which taketh strangers instead of her husband! 33 They give gifts to all whores: but thou givest thy gifts to all thy lovers, and hirest them, that they may come unto thee on every side for thy whoredom. 34 And the contrary is in thee from other women in thy whoredoms, whereas none followeth thee to commit whoredoms: and in that thou givest a reward, and no reward is given unto thee, therefore thou art contrary."

16.7.1.en: After the Lord had given the soul all these possibilities, she betrays Him, as He says to her: "But thou didst trust in thine own beauty, and playedst the harlot because of thy renown, and pouredst out thy fornications on every one that passed by; his it was" [15].

16.7.2.en: Here He speaks of spiritual adultery, which is the soul's turning aside after a bridegroom other than her own, and her attachment to temporal things at the expense of her relationship with God. Concerning this Origen says: [Adultery in its wide sense includes all forms of sin, for there is adultery in the sense that the soul enters into a mutual relationship with the Lord the Word and is united with Him in a kind of marriage, then is corrupted and defiled by another, who is the enemy of Him who reigned over her by faith, the Word of God, who is the Lord Jesus, the Bridegroom and spouse of the chaste and pure soul. As the Apostle says: "For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ" (2 Cor 11:2). So as long as the soul is united with her Bridegroom, and hears His words and clings to Him, she receives from Him the fruit of the Word... If the soul conceives from the works of Christ, she bears children, concerning whom it was said to her: "She shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety" (1 Tim 2:15)... Truly blessed is this fruitful soul that has shared in begetting the Word of the Lord and responded in His embrace; by this she bears genuine offspring, and out of her come purity, righteousness, patience, meekness, love and every noble progeny. But if the soul is wretched and leaves the holy bed of the Word of God and enters into the embraces of corruption, and is deceived by the error of the devil and the demons, she certainly bears, but she brings forth children of whom it is written that they are corrupt and imperfect, "the seed of the bed of the hypocrite they will cast out"].

16.7.3.en: Origen sees that adultery here means leaving the marriage home or going out from the holy family... Thus sinners by their spiritual adultery remain outside the tent of the Lord, while the saints are inside it.

16.7.4.en: Whoever is attached to the word of the Lord and walks in obedience to it lives as in the spiritual marriage home, but whoever is attached to false philosophies deprives himself of the heavenly wedding and is counted an adulterer.

16.7.5.en: This is the spiritual adultery which the soul commits by leaving God, her Bridegroom, and taking refuge in the devil and his ways. The features of this spiritual adultery are:

16.7.6.en: a. Pride: "But thou didst trust in thine own beauty, and playedst the harlot because of thy renown, and pouredst out thy fornications on every one that passed by; his it was" [15]. The beginning of the fall is pride, where man relies on his human arm and thinks himself to be something, so the grace of God forsakes him and he becomes a plaything of every sin. St. Isaac the Syrian says: [He who loves honor cannot escape the sicknesses of disgrace]. And St. Moses the Black says: [He who believes himself to be without fault has contained within himself all faults]. And Father Gregory (the Great) says: [Truly the soul that trusts in her beauty and thinks herself righteous plays the part of the harlot because of her fame, for in what she does well she does not do it to proclaim the glory of her Creator but seeks her own glory].

16.8.0.en: b. Defilement of the body: "And of thy garments thou didst take, and deckedst thy high places with divers colours, and playedst the harlot thereupon" [16]. If garments in the Holy Bible point to the body, then God punishes the man who makes of his body high places, that is, places of evil, on which sacrifices are offered to idols, so that Satan finds many places for himself in the body, through the eye, the ear, the hand, the belly... Our good body is turned into instruments of iniquity unto death. Therefore the Apostle says: "Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God" (Rom 6:13), "For as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness" (Rom 6:19). "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service" (Rom 12:1).

16.9.0.en: c. Defilement of God's holy things: "Thou hast also taken thy fair jewels (thy glory) of my gold and of my silver, which I had given thee, and madest to thyself images of men, and didst commit whoredom with them" [17]. Thus the Lord punishes His bride, not only because she is unfaithful, but because she took His riches and His holy things to use in her betrayal of Him.

16.9.1.en: Origen says: [She took the things from which is made what is for her glory and pride, which Moses wrote about in the Book of Numbers, the censers and cups and the golden lampstand... and she melted all these down and made for herself images of men for corruption and adultery, so her soul became an adulteress. This is the literal interpretation; but the symbolic one, as Origen sees it, is the replacement of the concepts of the word of God with counterfeit meanings, so the wicked melt down the divine Word which was given them for their glory and exchange the truth for falsehood, and God for other forms... God gave us the Law and the Prophets for our inner glory, but we misuse them. She uses His gold and His silver [17] and His oil and His incense [18] and His bread and all the food He gave her of fine flour and oil and honey! The ungrateful soul takes the gold of Christ and His silver to make images for herself with them, that is, she uses the heavenly things (the gold) and His Gospel word (the silver), not to lift the soul up to the divine life but to serve temporal thoughts. Faith becomes for her not union with God but a means to earthly ends.

16.9.2.en: We mention by way of example the drive of love which God gives to mankind and develops in the life of the believer... but some turn love into fleshly lusts, so the gift of God is used for the kingdom of darkness.

16.9.3.en: What he says of love applies to anger, for it is a gift by which man compels himself against sin, but some use it to be angry at others.

16.10.0.en: "And tookest thy broidered garments, and coverest them" [18].

16.10.1.en: What are these beautiful garments adorned with colors but the bowels of mercy, humility, patience and forbearance of others... This is the adornment with which the believer is adorned and covered.

16.10.2.en: Origen says: [The heretic mixes his soul-destroying philosophy with deceptive outward adornments, so that he bears the likeness of purity, chastity and meekness in order to hunt the simple into the destruction that ruins their whole life, and he is like one who covers idols with beautiful adornment.

16.10.3.en: [Let us be very watchful of the heretics who appear as if in a perfect life... for Satan, like a fowler of birds, makes a bait to catch the birds easily, offering them tempting food.

16.10.4.en: Satan has a kind of purity and meekness... to entice the human soul so that with false words he may catch it in his net and his various snares, for Satan strives to make man lose everything].

16.10.5.en: Again he says: [Satan accomplishes everything that appears good... and mixes and confuses matters in order to destroy human nature. Whoever is careful about the salvation of his soul does not rush after these deceptions].

16.10.6.en: "And thou hast set mine oil and mine incense before them" [18].

16.10.7.en: The literal meaning is that instead of using the oil and incense for the golden lampstand and the golden altar of incense, they were used in idolatrous worship. The oil points to the anointing of the Spirit, and the incense to the prayers of the saints, as though, instead of enjoying the leading of the Holy Spirit and the lifting up of the heart in prayer so that the believer may enjoy fellowship with God in His Son Jesus Christ by the Holy Spirit, his worship turns into pleasing men, so that they become those to whom he is devoted... He loses the holiest and most precious things through this slavery... slavery to vainglory and seeking the praise of others. The Lord's oil and incense point to worship, which, instead of being a spiritual ladder to rise toward the eternal things, becomes formalities that serve its own selfish interests.

16.11.0.en: As for the kinds of food, they are the divine gifts which God offers her, and she turns them aside from their spiritual goal: "My meat also which I gave thee, fine flour, and oil, and honey, wherewith I fed thee, thou hast even set it before them for a sweet savour" [19]. What is this food that God offers us but His word in the two Testaments? The Law and the Prophets are the fine flour, or the choice meal, and the New Testament is the honey. The word of God in the Old Testament is our bread on which we feed; without it we could not have known our Christ in the New Testament, who is "the desire of all nations," the honey of sweet taste in the depths of the soul! But the heretics use even the word of God, the spiritual food, to corrupt the minds of the simple!

16.11.1.en: How hard it is indeed for God to see that the very means of salvation, spiritual growth and union with Him are used to destroy the relationship with Him, and are even used on behalf of His enemy!

16.12.0.en: d. Destruction of the powers of the soul and body: "Thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured... Thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them" [20-21]. The people did this literally when they offered their children, who are God's children, and slew them and made them pass through the fire in idolatrous worship. Mothers would take their newborn children and offer them as sacrifices to the god Moloch. The priests would receive them, and to the sound of loud drums they would throw them onto the arms of the god, made of bronze heated with fire, so that no one would hear the cries of the children, but everyone would dance with delight and commit adultery... as worship of the god!! Children who should have been brought up as children of God, sanctified in the truth, were offered as sacrifices to Satan! Symbolically, the sons and daughters whom we bear to the Lord and then turn and slay for Satan's sake are the powers of the soul and body which are sanctified by the Holy Spirit, and then we turn back and defile them with wicked abominations. The believer, receiving love from the hand of the Lord so that his heart may be enlarged with love for God and men, sometimes turns it aside so that it becomes a fleshly lust serving his selfish ends for the sake of the enemy of good. So all the impulses of the soul and its inclinations and powers, which the Holy Spirit kindles so that they become like sons and daughters of God working within the heart for His sake, when they turn aside, become servants of the kingdom of darkness.

16.13.0.en: e. Her turning into idol temples: "Thou hast also built unto thee an eminent place, and hast made thee an high place in every street. Thou hast built thy high place at every head of the way, and hast made thy beauty to be abhorred... etc." [24-25]. Instead of the soul being a holy temple for God to dwell in, she becomes the dome of Satan, and sets up a place for him in all her life. She puts up high places for Satan in all her streets; wherever she goes she has no thought but for the pleasures of the flesh and the love of the world. At the head of every way she builds a high place, in her family life or her work or her social relationships... She does not think of what is God's but of what is sin's.

16.13.1.en: She has made abominable her beauty which God created, and as Origen says: [The human soul is very beautiful, her beauty is wonderful, because God created her, saying: "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness." What beauty is more excellent than this image and this likeness? But some paltry adulterers are attracted to her beauty and desire to corrupt her... Therefore the wise Paul says: "But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ" (2 Cor 11:3)...].

16.13.2.en: He also says: [The heretics corrupt the beauty of the soul and the mind by their false thoughts, for the soul falls into a spiritual adultery that corrupts her].

16.14.0.en: f. She sins without being satisfied: "Thou hast also committed fornication with the Egyptians thy neighbours, great of flesh; and hast increased thy whoredoms, to provoke me to anger... Thou hast played the whore also with the Assyrians, because thou wast unsatiable; yea, thou hast played the harlot with them, and yet couldest not be satisfied. Thou hast moreover multiplied thy fornication in the land of Canaan unto Chaldea; and yet thou wast not satisfied herewith" [26-29]. Although Egypt and Assyria were opposed to each other, the Jews at that time were in a state of dissatisfaction, accepting the gods of Egypt and at the same time the gods of Assyria, like the man in whose life sin has turned into a sickly condition, who sins to the right and to the left without aim and without satisfaction. He commits opposite sins at one time, as when a man falls into the sin of pride and self-importance and at the same time his heart is inflamed with evil lusts... "How weak is thine heart, saith the Lord GOD!" [30].

16.15.0.en: g. She sins without shame: the Lord likened her to "an imperious whorish woman" [30], who commits sin without shame, for she invites others and does not ask for hire but offers gifts and bribes: "They give gifts to all whores: but thou givest thy gifts to all thy lovers, and hirest them, that they may come unto thee on every side for thy whoredom" [33]. A man may justify his committing of wrong by his need or want for the sake of his material or social interests... but when a man becomes accustomed to sin he commits it at the expense of his health or his material or social interest...

16.15.1.en: When St. John Chrysostom wrote to his friend Theodore, who had fallen into fornication and broken the vow of virginity, and wished to lift him out of despair, in this chapter there is a living picture of the love of God, which calls fornicators in this hideous state to return to Him.

16.15.2.en: St. Jerome sees in one of his letters in this description a symbolic picture of the idle soul, without work, which leaves itself as a field for evil in every place and in every kind. Therefore he warns us against the idle life, saying: [In Egypt the monasteries laid down a rule not to receive anyone who does not wish to work, for they look to work not only as a necessity for the needs of the body but for the salvation of the soul. Do not let your mind wander in vain thoughts, lest it be like Jerusalem in her adultery, opening her feet to every one that passed by (Ezek 16:25)].

16.15.3.en: Origen offers us a symbolic interpretation of the imperious whorish woman who commits adultery without shame... She represents the religious man who sins and yet remains religious in appearance. The wicked man commits spiritual adultery and confesses his adultery with shame, but the religious man commits adultery and in shamelessness bears the appearance of a religious man.

16.15.4.en: What are the gifts which the harlot offers her lovers? She takes what belongs to her husband and offers it to the adulterers. This is what the heretics do when they misunderstand the word of God and His gifts, and use them for the sake of the kingdom of the enemy of good.

16.16.0.en: 35 "Wherefore, O harlot, hear the word of the LORD: 36 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thy brass was spent, and thy nakedness discovered through thy whoredoms with thy lovers, and with all the idols of thy abominations, and by the blood of thy children, which thou didst give unto them; 37 Behold, therefore I will gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure, and all them that thou hast loved, with all them that thou hast hated; I will even gather them round about against thee, and will discover thy nakedness unto them, that they may see all thy nakedness. 38 And I will judge thee, as women that break wedlock and shed blood are judged; and I will give thee blood in fury and jealousy. 39 And I will also give thee into their hand, and they shall throw down thine eminent place, and shall break down thy high places: they shall strip thee also of thy clothes, and shall take thy fair jewels, and leave thee naked and bare. 40 They shall also bring up a company against thee, and they shall stone thee with stones, and thrust thee through with their swords. 41 And they shall burn thine houses with fire, and execute judgments upon thee in the sight of many women: and I will cause thee to cease from playing the harlot, and thou also shalt give no hire any more. 42 So will I make my fury toward thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry. 43 Because thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, but hast fretted me in all these things; behold, therefore I also will recompense thy way upon thine head, saith the Lord GOD: and thou shalt not commit this lewdness above all thine abominations. 44 Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter. 45 Thou art thy mother's daughter, that lotheth her husband and her children; and thou art the sister of thy sisters, which lothed their husbands and their children: your mother was an Hittite, and your father an Amorite. 46 And thine elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters that dwell at thy left hand: and thy younger sister, that dwelleth at thy right hand, is Sodom and her daughters. 47 Yet hast thou not walked after their ways, nor done after their abominations: but, as if that were a very little thing, thou wast corrupted more than they in all thy ways. 48 As I live, saith the Lord GOD, Sodom thy sister hath not done, she nor her daughters, as thou hast done, thou and thy daughters. 49 Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and the peace of security was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy. 50 And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good. 51 Neither hath Samaria committed half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine abominations more than they, and hast justified thy sisters in all thine abominations which thou hast done."

16.16.1.en: a. Her open chastening: We have already spoken of how God covers our sins and advises us secretly that we may take advice, for our persistence in error allows open chastening, not for exposure but for discipline (chapter 5). Here, since in her adultery she has become "an imperious whorish woman" [30] and has entered a sickly state, never satisfied with sin and never ceasing to commit it with every one that passes by, the Lord is obliged, in order to discipline her, to intervene with her with some severity for the sake of her salvation, as He says: "Behold, therefore I will gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure, and all them that thou hast loved, with all them that thou hast hated; I will even gather them round about against thee, and will discover thy nakedness..." [37].

16.17.0.en: b. He leaves corruption to destroy itself, for those in whom she found her pleasure are the ones who destroy her life. "I will also give thee into their hand, and they shall throw down thine eminent place, and shall break down thy high places: they shall strip thee also of thy clothes, and shall take thy fair jewels, and leave thee naked and bare" [39].

16.17.1.en: The things which man thinks to be the object of his happiness become the very secret of his misery, and what he thinks to be the secret of his satisfaction he finds in the end to be the secret of his hunger and thirst and nakedness and shame!

16.18.0.en: c. The wrath of the Lord against her: When man rushes toward evil, not only does evil itself become a punishment to him, but he is deprived of being with God and falls under the divine wrath. But the bitterest and harshest degree of the divine wrath is that God "will be no more angry" [42], that is, He ignores her completely. If God is angry with us, it is because He loves us and desires our union with Him. But when we persist in rejecting Him, He no longer becomes angry, and we lose all divine love. "So will I make my fury toward thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry" [42].

16.18.1.en: Concerning this St. Jerome says: [The most severe degree of God's wrath against sinners is when He does not show anger... "For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth" (Heb 12:6). The father guides his son, and the teacher does not correct the way of his pupil if he does not love him, when he sees in him signs of fidelity. When the physician stops caring for the patient, that is a sign that he despairs of him]. He also says: [In other words, when you were merely a harlot I loved you with a love full of jealousy, but now that you have many lovers and I am despised by you, I will no longer be angry with you. In the same way a man is jealous over his wife when he loves her, but if he is not jealous over her it is because he hates her. So He does not say the words (of God) "I will visit their transgression with the rod" (Ps 89:33), but He says "I will not punish your daughters when they commit whoredom" (Hos 4:14)].

16.19.0.en: d. She becomes a byword: "Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter" [44]. When the believer falls into evil he is often worse than the unbeliever, because he takes what is God's, with the strong possibilities given to him, and uses it for evil, and therefore becomes a proverb before many. Here the people are reproached for having left God as their Father. Their mother became a Hittite and their father an Amorite through their relationship to them by sharing with them in their evil, and their sister became Samaria (Israel or the northern kingdom), which rushed into evil for a long time, and their younger sister Sodom, which deserved to be burned with fire, yet she became more wicked than all these, as He says: "Yet hast thou not walked after their ways, nor done after their abominations: but, as if that were a very little thing, thou wast corrupted more than they in all thy ways" [47].

16.20.0.en: He concentrates on the following sins [49]: 1. Pride [49-50] drives to revolt against God and disobedience... the end of pride is a fall. Origen says: [What then are the greatest of all sins? Surely those which caused the fall of Satan. What is this sin that caused the collapse of that greatness, of which the Apostle says: "Lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil" (1 Tim 3:6)? Arrogance, pride and haughtiness are the sins of Satan; because of them he left heaven and came down to the earth. Therefore: "God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble" (Jas 4:6).

16.20.1.en: Why should he who is dust and ashes be proud, so that man behaves arrogantly, forgetting what his end will be, forgetting that he is a fragile vessel, ignoring the filth in which he is sunk and the waste that comes out of his body?].

16.20.2.en: Origen rebukes proud priests, saying: [How quickly they forgot humility when they were appointed priests! As though they had been ordained in order to cease from humility, whereas they ought to have walked in the way of humility, for the Scripture says: "The greater you are, so increase in humility" (Sir 3:18). The congregation chooses you and you bow your head; they made you a leader, so do not exalt yourself, be among them as one of them. You must be humble and lowly and flee from pride, for it is the source of evils]. 2. Fulness of bread [49], where man seeks material satiety and relies on temporal things, despising all spiritual values. 3. The peace of security [49]: or the calming of conscience... Instead of confessing the fault and offering repentance, man quiets down and says to himself: Peace...; that is, choosing the broad way and the pampered life instead of repentance and bearing the Cross.

16.21.0.en: 52 "Thou also, which hast judged thy sisters, bear thine own shame for thy sins that thou hast committed more abominable than they: they are more righteous than thou: yea, be thou confounded also, and bear thy shame, in that thou hast justified thy sisters. 53 When I shall bring again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, then will I bring again the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them: 54 That thou mayest bear thine own shame, and mayest be confounded in all that thou hast done, in that thou art a comfort unto them. 55 When thy sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their former estate, and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former estate, then thou and thy daughters shall return to your former estate. 56 For thy sister Sodom was not mentioned by thy mouth in the day of thy pride, 57 Before thy wickedness was discovered, as at the time of thy reproach of the daughters of Syria, and all that are round about her, the daughters of the Philistines, which despise thee round about. 58 Thou hast borne thy lewdness and thine abominations, saith the LORD."

16.21.1.en: "Thou also, which hast judged thy sisters, bear thine own shame...

16.21.2.en: Yea, be thou confounded also, and bear thy shame, in that thou hast justified thy sisters. When I shall bring again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, then will I bring again the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them...

16.21.3.en: Shall return to their former estate" [52-55].

16.21.4.en: Origen observed that the way of return to the former state, that is, the state before the captivity, requires bearing shame and feeling ashamed of the wrong and abominations that man has committed. In his comment on the preceding words he says:

16.21.5.en: [No shameful deed ought to be practiced, but everything that is good by nature should be directed to God in true confidence. But since we as men sin much... we must be ashamed, lowering our eyes in humility because of our crimes, and not come forward with a brazen face like one who has never sinned in anything.

16.21.6.en: For it is better for a man to feel shame after he has sinned, especially since the deceiver, the maker of evils, often makes the sinner behave as though he were in the right instead of remembering the punishment that is due. We can see and learn from daily life how many people, after committing their sins, do not repent of what they did, but defend their corruption in vain... Therefore it was said: "Yea, be thou confounded also..." Do not think that this word was said to Jerusalem alone, but it was said to each one of us, who strip ourselves of faults. "Let him examine everything he has thought... he deserves shame before the searcher of hearts and reins (Ps 7:10); then he will be ashamed when he discerns exactly his thoughts, deeds and words... and hears the word of the prophet: be thou confounded... For confusion follows shame. Whoever practices a deed that deserves shame, God makes him ashamed, and says to him: 'Be thou confounded'].

16.21.7.en: If God commands Jerusalem to bear her shame and be ashamed, it is in order that she may confess the abominations she has committed, and by repentance He restores her from the state of disgrace to honor, restores her from her captivity to her homeland, as He says: "When I shall bring again their captivity... shall return to their former estate"

16.21.8.en: Origen comments on this by saying:

16.21.9.en: [It is a disgrace for a citizen to be exiled from his homeland...

16.21.10.en: The just Judge understands this and says to him who commits shameful deeds: Do not receive your exile with grief, O you who deserve punishment, for your murmuring against the punishment makes you unworthy of mercy; rather understand that you deserve the torment you are suffering. And when you humble yourself and acknowledge the justice of the sentence passed upon you, you can receive mercy from Him who is able, after your condemnation, to restore you to your former state, just as a great ruler can release those on an island or in exile or in prison; so much the more can the God of the universe restore the former honor to him who lost it, on condition that he confess his sin and that he deserves the sufferings he endures].

16.21.11.en: Origen gives a practical example in the Church, if a man is excommunicated from the Church, whether from the priesthood or the people. If he stirs up the people he drags the wicked after him and they treasure up for themselves wrath (Rom 2:5). But if he accepts that in complete humility, whether his excommunication is just or unjust, leaving the judgment to God, bearing the sentence patiently, he receives mercy from God and often returns to his former state (membership of the Church) in greater glory and honor.

16.21.12.en: When we are ashamed and confounded here, we move in the age to come "the tender mercy of our God" (Lk 1:78), and shame is taken away from us, but whoever murmurs here falls into eternal disgrace or shame.

16.22.0.en: Origen also observed that the return from captivity to the former state takes place according to the condition of man... It began with Sodom and her daughters, then Samaria and her daughters, and finally Jerusalem and her daughters [55]. For whoever knows more is beaten more. Gentile Sodom has less knowledge than Samaria (the heretics), and the knowledge of Samaria is less than that of Jerusalem.

16.22.1.en: [The nearer we draw to God... the farther we are from Him if we sin, and so we approach more terrible torments, for the judgment of God is just, "for the lowly is pardoned through mercy, but the mighty shall be mightily tormented" (Wis 6:7). He who was very small (1 Cor 15:9) deserves swift mercy].

16.22.2.en: Origen comments on the words of Scripture: "And thine elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters that dwell at thy left hand: and thy younger sister, that dwelleth at thy right hand, is Sodom and her daughters" [46], saying: [As virtue makes me a brother of the Lord Christ, so malice (evil) gains me many sisters, all of them sinners. When Jerusalem began to incline to sin, she did not yet have Samaria as a sister nor her sister Sodom, but when she went deeper into crime... she came to be in the midst of her two sisters, the elder Samaria and the younger Sodom].

16.22.3.en: To show the extent of Jerusalem's abominations, He made clear that by the abominations she had committed she justified her sisters, such as Samaria, as He says:

16.22.4.en: "Neither hath Samaria committed half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine abominations more than they, and hast justified thy sisters in all thine abominations which thou hast done...

16.22.5.en: They are more righteous than thou" [51-52].

16.22.7.en: [Indeed Samaria and Sodom were justified by the abominations of Jerusalem... Let us take care, for on the day of judgment those who are less wicked than we will judge us while we condemn others. Only One is justified before all, and no one is justified before Him. Sodom is justified by Jerusalem, who committed more abominations than she, and perhaps Jerusalem will be justified by another city more wicked than she...
